Foundation vs Instruction Tuned Models
Foundation
● Coherent, fluent generation
● Completion and continuation
● Vast world knowledge
● Potentially harmful outputs
● Difficult to control
● Misaligned with our values
Instruction Tuned
● Foundation ability and more
● Controllable by prompt
● Less need to fine-tune
● Follows any command 
● Slight hit to performance
● Sensitive to prompt template
[Slide 5]
Instruction Tuning
 Before Instruction Tuning:
– Trained to minimise next-token prediction loss on large corpora
– Not explicitly trained to follow user instructions
 Motivation for Instruction Tuning:
– Reduce mismatch between training objective and user intent
– Used to provide useful information and reliably respond to 
instructions

HHH - Guiding Principles
●Helpful
o Comprehend user's intentions
o Execute requested actions correctly
o Offers relevant supporting information and alternate solutions
●Honest
o Provide truthful, meaningful and specific information
o Admits when it is unable to produce relevant or correct information
o Advertises when a hypothesis is presented instead of fact
●Harmless
o Generated content does not contain offensive terminology or ideology
o Avoids providing information on potentially dangerous activities
o Refuses to participate in unlawful activities
o Can detect attempts to deceive and manipulate to extract illicit information

cause collapse?

Reasoning Models
[Slide 24]
● Prompt encourages the model to "think step by step" - turns hard 
task into series of simple tasks
● Key benefits: 
 Improves accuracy on complex reasoning tasks
 Creates transparent, verifiable solutions
 Reduces common reasoning errors
● Example:
Solve 13×27: First multiply 7×3=21, carry 2, then 7×1=7+2=9, so 
13×7=91. Next 20×13=260. Finally, 260+91=351.
[19] Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning 
in Large Language Models
Chain-of-Thought Prompting
[Slide 25]
● Two stages:
o Reasoning/thinking step
o Response
<think> Chain of thought reasoning for task. </think> Final 
response.
● Model can spend arbitrary time exploring different ideas
● Typically, the longer spent “thinking”, the better the 
performance

[Slide 29]
Summary
 Transformers + Self-Supervised Training
– Large-scale next-token prediction enables powerful general language 
representations.
 Instruction Tuning
– Converts raw pretrained models into useful assistants by training on instruction–
response pairs.
 Human Alignment (RLHF, PPO, DPO)
– Aligns model behaviour with human preferences, safety, and helpfulness.
 Mixture of Experts (MoE)
– Improves scalability and efficiency through sparse expert routing.
 Reasoning Models 
– Techniques such as Chain-of-Thought improve structured reasoning and problem-
solving.

[Slide 31]
The Problems with Prompt-Based Evaluation
“Evaluating generated text is now about as hard as 
generating it!”
 Human evaluation is the gold standard but could suffer from 
inconsistency, bias, and lack of standardisation
 LLM-based evaluation is much more scalable but highly sensitive to 
prompt design
– Even small prompt changes can lead to large performance differences
Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Inversion Learning for Highly Effective NLG Evaluation Prompts, https:// arxiv.org/pdf/2504.21117
[Slide 32]
High Sensitivity of LLMs to Prompt Design
 LLM-based evaluation is highly sensitivity to prompts, which 
are mostly hand-crafted
 Small design changes can significantly affect output quality
– E.g. Subtle variations in few-shot templates led to up to 76-point 
accuracy shifts (Polo et al., 2024)
 Performance varies with prompt phrasing, order, numerical 
scales and implicit biases
Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Inversion Learning for Highly Effective NLG Evaluation Prompts, https:// arxiv.org/pdf/2504.21117

[Slide 38]
Inversion Learning
 Study the problem of generating high-quality, model-specific 
evaluation prompts
 Core idea: learns an effective reverse mapping from model 
outputs back to their input instructions
 Requires only one evaluation sample (content + human score) 
to generate an evaluation prompt
Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Inversion Learning for Highly Effective NLG Evaluation Prompts, https:// arxiv.org/pdf/2504.21117

Conclusion
 Inversed instruction tuning for automatically generating high-quality, 
model-specific evaluation prompts via inversion learning
 Efficient high-quality prompts generation from a single evaluation 
sample
 Experiments across two LLM families, three evaluation tasks, and 
four datasets confirms that model-specific prompts are essential for 
effective LLM-based evaluation
